fields.headline: From operating requirements to a design that can move forward
fields.lead: We design newbuilds and vessel conversions, and we take on specialist calculations where a full design package is not required. The work can cover principal dimensions, hull form, hydrostatics, stability, resistance, structures, propulsion and technical drawings.

fields.heading: Different projects need different levels of design support
fields.intro: A new vessel, a conversion and a single calculation do not need the same scope. We start from the operating goal and the information already available, then define the work that actually needs to be done.

items.problem: I need a new vessel concept from an operating brief
items.context: The vessel type, mission, operating area or key constraints are known, but there is not yet a complete technical concept.
items.solution: We develop the principal dimensions, hull form, general arrangement, structure and propulsion concept from the operating requirements, then carry the agreed design into the calculations and drawings needed for the next stage.

items.problem: An existing vessel needs to be lengthened, reconfigured or repowered
items.context: Changes to dimensions, loading, layout or equipment can affect stability, structures and onboard systems.
items.solution: We review the available drawings and vessel condition, identify the areas affected by the proposed change, and define the calculations and drawings that need to be updated.

items.problem: I only need one calculation or design check
items.context: The project already has a design, but a specific question remains around stability, resistance, power, propellers, shafting or structural strength.
items.solution: We can take on a defined calculation package without rebuilding work that is already complete, giving the project the technical evidence needed to make the next decision.

items.problem: I already have drawings and need missing technical work completed
items.context: Part of the design package exists, but some calculations, drawings or supporting documents are still missing.
items.solution: We review the existing material, identify the gaps and complete the agreed technical work so the project can continue without duplicating what has already been done.

fields.heading: We can take on a complete design package or a defined part of the work
fields.caption: Some projects start from an operating brief. Others already have vessel data, drawings or a partial design. We adapt the scope to the actual starting point rather than forcing every project into the same process.

steps.desc: We look at the operating requirements, existing drawings and the intended use of the final output, then agree the work that needs to be done.

fields.heading: Common questions before a ship-design project starts
fields.intro: You do not need a complete specification to start a conversation. The questions below explain what information is useful, how narrowly the work can be scoped, and how we handle revisions.

items.title: Can you start if I do not have all the vessel parameters yet?
items.content: Yes. The vessel type, operating mission, expected dimensions, operating area or existing drawings are enough to begin. We will identify which missing inputs matter before detailed calculations start.

items.title: Can I engage you for one calculation instead of a full design package?
items.content: Yes. We can take on a defined calculation or drawing package for stability, resistance, power, propellers, shafting, structures or other clearly scoped design work.

items.title: Do you work on conversions of vessels already in service?
items.content: Yes. We review the existing vessel information and the proposed change, then identify which parts of the design are affected and need to be recalculated or redrawn.

items.title: Can you revise the design after owner or yard feedback?
items.content: Yes. For the work within our agreed scope, we can review technical feedback and update the calculations or drawings when the project changes.

items.title: What determines the project schedule?
items.content: Timing depends on vessel type, the quality of the available input data, the number of calculations and drawings required, and how much iteration the design needs. We confirm an expected schedule after reviewing the brief.

fields.heading: Existing information is enough to start
fields.description: Vessel type, operating profile, expected dimensions, old drawings or photos of the current vessel can all be useful. Send what you have and we will tell you what can be done next and what additional information would help.
